newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore diesel weaker on lower regional demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore diesel weaker on lower regional demand.

text.p: Singapore diesel edged down slightly on Tuesday on lower gas oil futures seen in London and limited regional buying interest, traders said.
Gas oil swaps for November were traded down at $29.70 and $29.75 per barrel against Monday's close of $29.95/$30.05, brokers said.
The November/December gas oil spread widened to 50/60 cents from 30/40 cents on the expected arrival of arbitrage cargoes from the U.S. West Coast in end November, traders said.
The gas oil physical market was quiet in Singapore but some buying was seen from China for small lots on an ex-Hong Kong basis at around $240 per tonne, traders said.
Jet fuel was offered down on ample regional supplies and lacklustre buying from Japan with the last November arrival cargo traded a premium of about $1.55 to spot Singapore quotes.
An offer was seen at $30.40 a barrel for 100,000 barrels loading November 20-24, 10 cents below Monday's offer.
The November jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) was quoted at 20/30 cents down from Monday's 20/40 cents. December regrade traded at 75 cents.
Gasoline traders assessed the prompt market as firm with supplies tight until end November. Only one Chinese cargo of 90-octane was heard available for November 16-30.

But December was said to be long with a 40,000 tonne-Chinese cargo of 93-octane unleaded lifting December 16-31 sold at $2 a barrel over Singapore spot naphtha quotes fob Zhenghai last Friday, lower than previous reports of $2.50-$3.00.

Regional demand in December is limited to Taiwan's usual monthly purchase tender which closes on Tuesday and a major in Australia is seeking 200,000 barrels in December. Singapore 95-octane unleaded offered to low of $24.60 a barrel fob.
